# Parity fixtures

`lines.reference.json` is the expected row output of the retired
[`vue-diff@1.2.4`](https://github.com/hoiheart/vue-diff) for a set of input pairs. It is
consumed by `src/core/diff/parity.spec.ts` to assert this library produces **byte-identical**
line/row structures, which is what makes the drop-in claim testable rather than aspirational.

Notably, parity holds even though the diff engine was swapped (`diff-match-patch` → `diff`).

## Shape

An array of cases:

```jsonc
{
  "p": "a\nb\nc\n",     // prev input
  "c": "a\nX\nc\n",     // current input
  "split": [ /* Lines[] as the original emits them */ ],
  "unified": [ /* Lines[] */ ]
}
```

## Regenerating

Generated by reimplementing the original's `renderLines` verbatim from its published source
(`src/utils.ts` in `vue-diff@1.2.4`) and running it under `diff-match-patch`. The original
is archived read-only, so this output is stable.

To regenerate, in a scratch directory:

```bash
npm install vue-diff@1.2.4 diff-match-patch
# port renderLines / getSplitLines / getUnifiedLines from vue-diff's src/utils.ts,
# run it over the case list, and write the JSON described above.
```

Only regenerate when a deviation from the original is **deliberate** — and record the reason
in the commit message. An unexplained fixture change silently discards the parity guarantee.
